pages.title: England 78-15 Japan: Will Joseph makes sensational Test comeback - BBC Sport
pages.description: Will Joseph's comeback after four years off the Test scene was worth waiting for. And there was plenty elsewhere to buoy England in a rout of Japan.
pages.text: England 78-15 Japan: Will Joseph makes sensational Test comeback - BBC Sport Figure caption, Highlights: Joseph scores five tries as England enjoy huge win against Japan By Mike Henson BBC Sport rugby union news reporter Published 14 November 2026 Eddie Jones aired a complaint about Twickenham's in-stadium experience when he appeared on BBC Radio 5 Live this week. "Being a spectator and being told when to make noise is a bit funny," said the Japan boss, objecting to a big-screen request for an increase in volume. Jones sat stony-faced in the coaching box as the message appeared again in the midst of his team's 78-15 thrashing at England's hands on Saturday. There was little for him to enjoy on his return to Twickenham, where he was head coach for seven years. But, for the rest of a capacity crowd, it was a fun one. With junior tickets on sale at £15, there was a different atmosphere from usual. The decibels were higher, the demographic was younger, the spirits a little lighter. And England brought plenty of entertainment to the party. Thirteen tries in total, with Will Joseph's five putting him in the centre of the chorus line. The 24-year-old won his only previous England cap under Jones. Back in the summer of 2022, he was a teenage apprentice taken on tour to Australia and thrust into the second Test as a last-minute replacement. His promise has taken some time to be fulfilled. pages.title: England 78-15 Japan: Will Joseph scores five as hosts rout Brave Blossoms - BBC Sport
pages.description: Will Joseph marked his comeback after four years out the Test game with a record-equalling five tries as England tore through Japan.
pages.text: England 78-15 Japan: Will Joseph scores five as hosts rout Brave Blossoms - BBC Sport Figure caption, Highlights: Joseph scores five tries as England enjoy huge win against Japan By Mike Henson BBC Sport rugby union news reporter at Allianz Stadium Published 14 November 2026 Nations Championship England (49) 78 Tries: Joseph 5, Steward, Genge, Murley, Earl, Martin, B Curry, M Smith, Fisilau Cons: Ford 4, Slade Pen: Ford Japan (10) 15 Tries: Dearns, Helu Con: Saito Pen: Saito Will Joseph marked his comeback after four years out the Test game with a record-equalling five tries as England tore through Japan and set their sights on New Zealand next weekend. A teenage Joseph made his debut as a late replacement in a game against Australia four years ago. Since then he has endured his boyhood club London Irish going bust, an underwhelming spell at Harlequins and the loss of hearing in his left ear after an auto-immune reaction. But his superb early season form for Gloucester has thrust him back into the international picture and he took his opportunity superbly, showing work-rate and intelligence as well as raw top-end speed. Four other players - Douglas Lambert, Rory Underwood, Josh Lewsey and Henry Arundell - have scored five tries in a single match for England. Japan were vastly over-matched, unable to rev up the ball movement and quickfire rucks that have made them a threat to the game's major powers in the past. pages.description: England risked throwing away a three-goal lead against Spain after Elliot Anderson was sent off, but held on for a thrilling 3-2 win in Madrid
pages.text: England fend off fiery Spain fightback after Anderson’s red to top Nations League group | Nations League | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Ezri Konsa gives England a 2-0 lead over Spain – but a rough ride to the final whistle followed for the visitors. Photograph: Francisco Seco/AP View image in fullscreen Ezri Konsa gives England a 2-0 lead over Spain – but a rough ride to the final whistle followed for the visitors. Photograph: Francisco Seco/AP Nations League England fend off fiery Spain fightback after Anderson’s red to top Nations League group David Hytner at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano Sun 15 Nov 2026 16.56 EST Last modified on Sun 15 Nov 2026 21.30 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google It was the game to show Thomas Tuchel where his rebooted England team had got to; surely the ultimate test in international football. Spain in Spain. A world champion team who, in Tuchel’s words, had “forgotten how to lose.” Before this Nations League group decider, they had been beaten only once in 43 matches – on penalties against Portugal in the final of this competition last year. What England produced for 65 minutes was extraordinary. What followed was equally so for different reasons. When it was over, England had made the most sensational of statements. Back in 2018, on their previous visit to Spain, England won 3-2 in Seville in the Nations League; it was one of Sir Gareth Southgate’s most famous results, an ignition point. pages.description: England confidently sweep aside Australia in the third one-day international in Hobart to seal a statement series win.
pages.text: England in Australia: Harry Brook's side win decider for statement series win - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, England have won four ODI series this year By Matthew Henry BBC Sport Journalist Published 18 November 2026 Third one-day international, Hobart England 328 (48.3 overs): Duckett 133, Jacks 59; Edwards 4-31 Australia 231 (46.5 overs): Renshaw 55; Baker 4-45 England won by 97 runs Scorecard England confidently swept aside Australia in the third one-day international in Hobart to seal a statement series win. At times the series decider felt inconsequential - the latest seismic turn in Australia's sandpaper scandal taking all attention during Australia's chase - but Harry Brook's side won by 97 runs in an important step as they build towards next year's World Cup. Even when failing to fully take advantage of a fast start, England reached 328 before being bowled out in the penultimate over, with Ben Duckett making a fine 133 from 115 balls. Duckett's century, after all of his struggles in last winter's Ashes, was his first for England on Australian soil. A 48-ball 59 from Will Jacks ensured his innings was not wasted as Australia's spinners slowed scoring through the middle. Just as impressive was another exciting effort from England's new-ball pair Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker. Atkinson dismissed Travis Head for the third time in a row in the first over - something to be noted before next year's Ashes series. The England forward is preparing for the Champions League clash on Tuesday following his summer move from Newcastle in a deal worth more than £69m. Gordon has helped Barca to the top of La Liga and has scored three goals in 13 appearances in all competitions, including one in Saturday's 6-1 win over Alaves. But the 25-year-old wants to do more to help Hansi Flick's side complete a clean sweep of trophies this season. "The challenge of joining Barca is different to what I've had before because I was fighting relegation for two or three years (at Everton), which was tough," he said. "At Newcastle we were fighting for the Champions League and to push up the table and now fighting for Barca for every trophy. "To be competing on every front for every trophy is definitely the most enjoyable. I think people think it's more pressure but it's actually less pressure than fighting relegation and fighting to push up the table for the Champions League. "I want to win every trophy. pages.text: England team news: Thomas Tuchel omits Jarrad Branthwaite, James Garner and Josh King for Spain game - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, James Garner played as a substitute against Croatia on Thursday, while Jarrad Branthwaite and Josh King were unused By Sami Mokbel Senior football correspondent Published 15 November 2026 England manager Thomas Tuchel has omitted Josh King, James Garner and Jarrad Branthwaite from his squad to face world champions Spain in Madrid on Sunday night. England travelled to Spain with a squad of 26 players but Uefa rules state that only 23 players can be selected in a matchday squad for Nations League games The return to fitness of Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence - who missed Thursday's win over Croatia - has been a contributing factor in the trio's omission. Arsenal defender Konsa could come straight back into the starting XI while James Trafford will replace Jordan Pickford in goal. Garner replaced Declan Rice in the 77th minute of the 2-1 victory over Croatia at Wembley, scoring a goal that was subsequently disallowed, while Everton team-mate Branthwaite and Fulham's King were unused substitutes. King received his first senior call-up for the two final Nations League fixtures in Group A3, but the midfielder, 19, will not feature in this international window. However, fellow first-time call-ups Jobe Bellingham and James Hill are included. The Bath man burst on to the international scene in a man-of-the-match display against Argentina at the end of 2025, but has not played for his country in the 12 months since. Ojomoh was initially left out of Steve Borthwick's wider training squad but after starring for the 'A' team has been catapulted back into the England number 12 shirt and with it World Cup contention. "Max is one of the most talented players in English rugby," boss Steve Borthwick told BBC Sport. In one of the great upsets of the professional era, New Zealand lost 35-28 in Cardiff at the weekend, a first defeat against the Welsh in 73 years. New Zealand will face an in-form England in Twickenham as they look to avoid back-to-back Nations Championship losses, with Rennie vowing not to brush the Wales result "under the carpet". "It's important we poke each other in the chest at the start of the week," Rennie said. "You have to front up and take things on the chin, all of us. Come Saturday, our mindset will be fully on England and our job is to perform. "We will be highly motivated for the weekend, but we won't brush the [Wales] result under the carpet. "[The players] are feeling it. They know we let ourselves down and we let the country down." A close-up of his own face on the Twickenham big screen. A painful inquest under the sticks. Jack van Poortvliet's first meeting with New Zealand was only four minutes old when it curdled sour. In November 2022 Van Poortvliet, then 21, was winning only his sixth cap. Sharing the scrum-half duties with England veterans Ben Youngs and Richard Wigglesworth, he had been a key part in Leicester's run to the Premiership title the previous season. Van Poortvliet was touted as the next big thing at Test level too. But, off an early England line-out, Van Poortvliet, focused on Owen Farrell's hands, failed to spot Dalton Papali'i flying up out of the line. The All Black flanker picked off the interception and cantered in for the game's opening try. Van Poortvliet's afternoon ended after 54 minutes. The Gloucester pivot has recovered from a hip knock and is set to return to the starting XV at number 12 for the visit of the wounded All Blacks. For Atkinson, this weekend's game comes a fortnight after he made his first Allianz Stadium appearance with England in the 45-22 thumping of Australia. "It's sort of ticking off wishes and dreams that you have as a young aspiring rugby player," Atkinson told BBC Sport. "Watching [England against New Zealand in 2012] when Manu [Tuilagi] scored that try and set up that try, the big performance in the semi-final of the World Cup a few years ago [in 2019]. "And obviously I was frustrated to not be available last year when the team put in a good performance. "So a lot of things spring to mind and to be able to be out there and show what I can do on that stage will be really exciting for me personally." pages.description: Sarina Wiegman says she "cannot think of a better job in football" as she commits to staying on as manager of the Lionesses until after Euro 2029.
pages.text: England women's manager Sarina Wiegman signs two-year contract extension - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Sarina Wiegman has been in charge of England for more than five years By Paul Battison BBC Sport Journalist Published 19 October 2026 England manager Sarina Wiegman has signed a two-year contract extension with the Lionesses. The 56-year-old's previous deal was due to expire after next summer's World Cup, but her new contract will run until the end of Euro 2029. Dutchwoman Wiegman guided England to their second straight European Championship title with victory over Spain in the Euro 2025 final. The victory meant the Lionesses became the first England team - women's or men's - to win a major trophy on foreign soil. "I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football," said Wiegman. "Working for a world-class organisation like The FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day." England thrashed Greece 8-1 on aggregate last week to qualify for round two of the World Cup play-offs, where they will face Ukraine. Should the Lionesses win that two-legged tie, they will qualify for next summer's World Cup in Brazil. "My main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come," Wiegman added. "We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year." Wiegman replaced Phil Neville

pages.text: England: Alessia Russo named women's player of the year - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Alessia Russo has scored 31 goals in 68 games for England By Paul Battison BBC Sport Journalist Published 11 October 2026 Forward Alessia Russo has been named England women's player of the year. The 27-year-old, who also won the award two seasons ago, has been a key player in the 2025-26 campaign, featuring in all 10 games and scoring five goals. She started nine of those games, including all six of England's 2027 World Cup qualifiers. Last week, she scored the third goal as England beat Greece 3-1 in their 2027 World Cup play-off semi-final first leg, with the second leg at Leicester's King Power Stadium on Tuesday. Arsenal's Russo pipped Chelsea pair Lucy Bronze and Hannah Hampton to the award, which is voted for by fans. "To receive the award is really special, particularly as it comes directly from the fans. I am so grateful for their support," said Russo. Russo is among 30 players who were nominated in September for the women's Ballon d'Or, with Alex Greenwood the only other English player on the shortlist. Figure caption, 'Russo needs to start as a nine for England' "A big thank you also to my team-mates - it is always about the collective," Russo added. Russo has represented England at every stage from under-15s level upwards and won her first senior international cap when she came on as a substitute against Spain in the final game of the 2020 SheBelieves Cup. William Shakespeare, "Hamlet" Celebrating the English language at the United Nations English Language Day at the United Nations is celebrated on the 23 rd of April — the date traditionally observed as both the birthday and date of death of William Shakespeare . As well as being the English language's most famous playwright, Shakespeare had a significant impact on modern-day English . Shakespeare's creativity with language meant he contributed hundreds of new words and phrases: 'gossip'; 'fashionable' and 'lonely' were all first used by Shakespeare. He also invented phrases like 'break the ice', 'faint-hearted' and 'love is blind'. English is one of the languages of international communication. People from different countries and cultures are increasingly able to communicate with each other in English, even if it is not their first language. This makes it an essential tool for global cooperation and diplomacy. At the United Nations, English is one of the two working languages, along with French. pages.text: English Standards English Standards Skip Navigation English Standards The U.S. Census Bureau’s Statistics in Schools (SIS) activities are based on relevant education standards and guidelines that outline the foundational knowledge and skills students should have at certain levels. The SIS activities — which are designed to supplement or guide, not replace, existing curricula — help develop these skills and knowledge. Not all educators use the same standards. For this reason, many of the activities address multiple standards and guidelines. ENGLISH LANGUAGE ARTS Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects These standards, published in 2010, were created by a group of educators and experts in various subjects. In 2009, the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and the Council of Chief State Schools Officers began developing the Common Core State Standards — sets of expected knowledge and skills that represent what K-12 students should know and be able to do in math and English language arts and literacy. The literacy standards can be integrated into any history and social studies curriculum. The Common Core State Standards are used by teachers across the nation. Forty-two states and the District of Columbia have adopted at least some of these standards. A naturally occurring geothermal system, known as a hydrothermal system , requires three key elements to generate electricity: heat, fluid, and permeability, which is when fluid can move freely through the underground rock. In many areas, however, the underground rock is hot but there is not enough natural permeability or fluids present. In those cases, an enhanced geothermal system (EGS) can be used to create a human-made reservoir to tap that heat for energy. In an EGS, fluid is injected deep underground under carefully controlled conditions to create new fractures and cause pre-existing fractures to re-open, creating permeability. Increased permeability allows fluid to circulate throughout the more fractured hot rock, and the fluid becomes hot as it circulates. Operators pump the hot water up to the surface, where it generates electricity for the grid. Watch a video to learn more about the steps and benefits in EGS development . With the outbreak of the Civil War in 1861, enslaved African Americans saw the war as opportunity to emancipate themselves. When President Lincoln authorized the Emancipation Proclamation, formerly enslaved African American men joined the Union army to fight for the full emancipation of their race. The conclusion of the war in Union victory and the ratification of the 13th, 14th, and 15th Amendments to the US Constitution brought African Americans closer than they ever had been to full citizenship. Environmental and Legacy Management The Office of Environmental Management’s (EM) mission is to complete the safe cleanup of environmental legacy waste resulting from decades of nuclear weapons development and nuclear energy research. Since its formation in 1989, the Environmental Management program has tackled one of the largest environmental cleanup efforts in the world — addressing decades of nuclear weapons production and government-sponsored nuclear energy research in the United States. DOE established the Office of Legacy Management on Dec. 15, 2003, to fulfill the department’s post-closure responsibilities by providing long-term surveillance and maintenance, records management, benefits continuity, property management, and land use planning. Presently, Legacy Management manages over 100 legacy sites in 29 states and Puerto Rico. pages.text: Environmental Sustainability Smithsonian Magazine Skip to main content Environmental Sustainability Sustainability means working to protect our natural resources for future generations. We understand that recycling is inherently good and is fundamental to a healthy environment and society. But it is important to separate the issue of improving collection rates from how that recycled material is then used. Simply dictating that recycled fiber should go into magazine paper overlooks the fact that it could be put to far more efficient and sustainable use in other products. In the past decade, the production of printing and writing papers in North American has dropped by nearly 50% at the same time that exports of recycled paper to China have increased significantly. As a result, despite overall increases in paper recovery rates in the United States, the availability of recycled fiber suitable for use in magazine grades has actually decreased. Given this growing shortage of suitable recycled fiber, it is important to insure that the recycled fiber that is available is put to the best use. It’s not always the right choice to say it should be used in every instance. For example, when recycled fiber is used in certain packaging materials (like recycled paperboard) nearly 100% of the recycled material can be used; however, when recycled fiber is used for magazine paper typically only 70% of the recycled material is usable. HHCB is a synthetic musk used widely in fragrances and in household products such as detergents, cleaners, and air fresheners. Because this chemical is used so broadly, EPA’s review needs to reflect the full body of available science and give the public an opportunity to review the same information EPA used in its draft assessment. Formaldehyde is a component of resins and adhesives used to make composite wood products such as plywood, particleboard, and medium-density fiberboard, which are found in furniture, cabinets, flooring, and building materials. The Formaldehyde Standards for Composite Wood Products Act of 2010 directed EPA to set emission limits for these products to reduce exposure and protect public health. Kriley first became the BLM’s Director of the Office of Law Enforcement and Security (OLES) in November 2020. In October 2021, Director Kriley was transferred to the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs as the Special Advisor for Law Enforcement and Justice Affairs. In August 2025, after a successful four years serving Indian Country, Kriley returned to the BLM OLES Director position. Kriley brings extensive law enforcement and leadership skills to the BLM from his more than 28 years in federal law enforcement. Kriley was a member of the U.S. Foreign Service serving as a Special Agent with the Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service for the first 23 years of his career before joining the Department of the Interior. Kriley’s overseas service included tours in Egypt, Kenya, Poland, and Afghanistan. Prior to entering the Foreign Service, Kriley was an Assistant Professor of Criminal Justice at a private college in Wisconsin and a Military Police Officer in the Unites States Army Reserves. Spent the morning with the Bicycle wiki page and a 300-post thread about access=dismount, and the same thing kept coming up: our cycling data is really good at describing the road, and a bit less good at describing the person on the bike. None of that is in the data, and it’s the part that matters on a Tuesday morning when it’s pouring. ERISA requires plans to provide participants with plan information including important information about plan features and funding; provides fiduciary responsibilities for those who manage and control plan assets; requires plans to establish a grievance and appeals process for participants to get benefits from their plans; and gives participants the right to sue for benefits and breaches of fiduciary duty. There have been a number of amendments to ERISA, expanding the protections available to health benefit plan participants and beneficiaries. One important amendment, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) , provides some workers and their families with the right to continue their health coverage for a limited time after certain events, such as the loss of a job. Another amendment to ERISA is the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act which provides important protections for working Americans and their families

In its final operating configuration, it will be covered and operate in vacuum. Very soon, the International System of Units (SI) may be revised to define the unit of mass in terms of a fixed value of the Planck constant, h . That move would end more than two centuries of dependence on an artifact standard kilogram that is very difficult to transfer and the mass of which drifts over time. It is not immediately obvious how mass is related to h , which is the constant used to determine the energy of a quantum mechanical entity such as a particle or wave. It is perhaps most familiar in the context of light, in the formulation E = hν, where E is energy (in joules) and ν is frequency. Mass, of course, does not appear explicitly in that equation, nor in the currently accepted value of the Planck constant: 6.62606X × 10 −34 joule second (J·s), where X is the final digit to be determined.
